Generating-function chapter

Scientific and visual audit: d_generating

Delivery status and declared scope

Complete English review draft, not student-approved. Standing user authorization permits sequential continuation after this chapter's audits. Website publication, GitHub mirroring and student approval are separate states.

The chapter has 31 main sections, including 26 teaching sections before its complete summary; two additional proof subsections; 82 complete worked problems; 80 full-sentence final reasoning rules; an editable exact laboratory; and precise references. Its declared scope covers formal power-series algebra, coefficient extraction and precision, shifts and residue projections, formal calculus and transforms, rational partial fractions with a basis justification, boundary-corrected recurrences, bounded and weighted inventories, compositions and partitions, Durfee and diagonal-hook bijections, Catalan branch selection, a proved formal coefficient-inversion theorem, EGF products and composition, label allocations, cycles and exclusions, distinguished labels, marked parameters, PGF moment hypotheses, and exact/asymptotic distinctions. General complex analytic singularity-transfer theory is explicitly outside the scope.

Written course selection and actual reading

Four complementary courses from four universities were selected after a documented nine-candidate search: MIT 6.042J, UC Berkeley Math 172, CMU 15-251 and Princeton Analysis of Algorithms / Analytic Combinatorics Part One. Actual reading covers MIT Chapter 15, one-based PDF pages 636–670; all Berkeley ordinary/exponential/partition notes (7, 10 and 9 pages); all nine CMU handout pages; and all 52 Princeton written slides at Robert Sedgewick's official author mirror. The audit distinguishes author names from unestablished lecture-instructor attribution.

Native Berkeley downloads have recorded hashes. CMU and Princeton were read through official web PDF text after native downloads timed out; no downloaded-file hash is fabricated. Damaged extracted mathematical glyphs were resolved through independent derivation. Source discrepancies addressed include the general-ring unit criterion, shifted Fibonacci boundaries, empty-component local finiteness, forced-recurrence pole degree, and the meaning of a binary-tree leaf. Candidate syllabus screening is not counted as reading a lecture.

The survey is bounded by accessible written materials and declared scope. It is not a ranking of every course offered worldwide. Original derivations and complete reconstructed solutions are supplied; entire copyrighted problem collections are not reproduced.

Problems, final rules and original examinations

Eighty authored or explicitly credited course-pattern reconstructions cover exact formulas, operator distinctions, initial-value counterexamples, rational cancellation, forcing, bounded counts, restricted partitions, formal inversion, label normalization, cycle restrictions and moments. Foundational diagnostic problems support the medium-to-hard bank; entries are not all mislabeled difficult.

Two authentic bridges revisit MSc CS 1405 Q130 and doctoral CS 1404 Q28. Both exact original PDF pages were re-rendered, visually read and matched to recorded source hashes. English adaptations preserve the problem's index range and data; solutions are independently derived, not described as official answer keys. Q130's prefix recurrence gives the OGF (1-x)/(1-2x). Q28 retains the constant forcing four and the shifted boundary values 1403 and 2025. Its generating-function extension agrees with those boundaries and the next two terms; the original parity-state method remains the faster exam solution.

The end-of-chapter section contains eighty complete, condition-bearing rules rather than fragments: what operation is valid, which hypotheses it uses, what alternative it must be distinguished from, and where common index or normalization errors arise. The complete summary is separate from the full lesson.

Independent mathematics

Every one of the eighty original/reconstructed answers has a recorded independent check. Checks use symbolic rational/series expansion, exact fractions, direct subset and tuple enumeration, actual permutations and their cycles, labelled set partitions, binary words and ordered binary trees. Exact comparisons include generalized-binomial signs, resonant and boundary formulas, cap complementation, unequal bounds, odd/distinct partitions, Durfee counts, coefficient inversion, pairings, restricted blocks, derangements, leaf statistics and PGF moments.

The JavaScript models were compared against independent references for 100 inputs and 781 generated checkpoints, including the five exact question-specific parameter variants. General arguments and all written solution domains were reviewed separately; finite checks supplement proofs rather than substitute for them. Advanced claims retain their field, invertibility, local-finiteness and analytic conditions.

Specialized diagrams and laboratories

Seventeen stored models contain 218 exact checkpoints and 23 mounted lesson/solution appearances. They show reciprocal cancellation, a convolution diagonal, residue filtering, capped distributions, unordered coin products, ordered compositions, partition-product rows, Ferrers/Durfee geometry, complete Dyck first returns, actual label allocations, binary-word marking, and a repeated-pole coefficient decomposition. Five additional scenarios use the exact question data rather than a loosely related sample.

Each complete-object enumeration explicitly distinguishes different objects from continuous physical time. Every table step adds a specified factor or contribution. Result/Before/Compare/original views, paused playback, backward steps, seeking, reduced motion and full printed checkpoints use the shared library controls. The editable laboratory displays a model-specific native MathML readout, and mathematical checks report actual coefficient or inventory conditions. The convolution view is 760 by 380; other stored stages are 760 by 350, within the 420-height limit. Mobile diagrams scroll inside their own frame without expanding the page.

Real-browser review and preservation

Edge loaded Source Sans 3, Newsreader, STIX Two Math and JetBrains Mono. All stored checkpoints passed the measured glyph-bound, text-overlap and padding checks. The assembled lesson contained 983 MathML elements after mounting solutions. Mathematical script bases do not attach to isolated closing delimiters; tested fences have nonzero glyph bounds; links have no underline. There were no runtime errors, undefined teaching fields or mobile page overflow.

Play/Pause, restart, previous steps, scrubbing, reduced motion, print checkpoints, twelve editable model scenarios and nine invalid-input preservation cases passed. Screenshots of the convolution grid, Ferrers diagrams, labels, binary marking, bounded counts, poles, final rules, worked solutions, mobile and print views were retained and manually inspected. The library has 51 chapter cards and the Week 4 link works. These results concern the tested browser and declared finite domains.
